title: Waterfall Trail & Schraubenfall Hintertux
name: Waterfall Trail & Schraubenfall Hintertux
kurzbeschreibung: The Wasserfallweg in Hintertux: a spectacular circular hiking trail to the roaring Kesselfall and Schraubenfall waterfalls featuring wooden bridges and natural rock basins.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wildly romantic Wasserfallweg Hintertux is located at the head of the Tuxertal valley in the municipality of Tux in Tyrol's Zillertal (Bezirk Schwaz) at an altitude of approximately 1,500 to 1,700 metres. Starting directly at the foot of the Hintertux glacier lift (Gletscherbahn Hintertux), this secured adventure trail reveals a breathtaking natural landscape of roaring cascades, deep glacial potholes, and millennia-old rock polish. The dramatic ensemble of the thunderous Kesselfall and the protected natural monument Schraubenfall is considered one of the most impressive natural spectacles in the entire Zillertal.

Schraubenfall, Kesselfall & Cave Trail

Along this approximately two-hour circular trail, hikers walk close to the foaming waters of the Tuxbach torrent, fed by the mighty glaciers of the Gefrorene Wand and the Olperer. Over masterfully constructed wooden boardwalks and secured rock paths, the trail first leads to the Kesselfall, which plunges with a thunderous roar into a deeply eroded rock cauldron. Shortly thereafter, walkers arrive at the famous Schraubenfall: here, the torrential meltwater has carved a corkscrew-shaped gorge deep into the hard slate rock. Small rock caverns and wooden viewing platforms afford dizzying downward vistas into the raging eddies. On sunny days, the fine mist in the gorge produces vivid rainbows and creates a refreshing microclimate.

Visit & Getting There

The Wasserfallweg Hintertux is freely accessible and free of charge during the snow-free season from early May until late October (closed in winter due to snow and ice hazards). Walking time for the entire circuit is around 1.5 to 2 hours. Getting there by car: Via the Inntalautobahn A12 (Zillertal exit), continuing on the B169 to Mayrhofen and along the Tuxer Landesstraße to the end of the valley in Hintertux (large free car park at the glacier lift valley station). By public transport: Zillertalbahn railway to Mayrhofen station, then by the hourly Tuxer Sportbus directly to the stop Hintertux Gletscherbahn right at the trailhead.

Tips

Sturdy hiking boots with non-slip treaded soles are strongly recommended due to damp rock and wooden steps; the trail is not suitable for prams. Combine the hike with a stop at traditional alpine inns in Hintertux or a cable car ride up the glacier into the realm of eternal ice.
